topic: A neighbor wants to install a fence
text: Good morn, neighbor. I've been thinkin' on your talk of a fence, and it don't sit light in my heart. This land, it's more than just dirt and crops. It’s the hands of our fathers, the sweat of our brows. But fences, they put lines where no lines should be. They say, “This is mine, that is yours,” when the good earth knows no such divides. We've always shared what grows, what we have, like in the years when the rain wouldn’t come and the hunger gnawed at our bellies. A fence might keep out the wandering sheep, aye, but it also keeps out the neighbor’s goodwill. Think on this, I say. Think of the Saint who taught us to share our harvests, not to hoard behind walls of wood. Let's talk more, you and I, over a cup of ale and the wisdom of ages.
